purpose: GitHub keeps listing a workflow as active for as long as one historical run exists, even after its file is gone from every ref. `gh workflow list` therefore shows names that nothing in this repository defines, and there is no way to tell those apart from a live workflow that simply has not fired yet - the 'exists but nothing invokes it' defect, seen from the outside. Every such name is recorded here with the decision behind it. validate_workflows.js asserts this file stays honest: an entry may not name a workflow file that is present on disk.

workflows.name: ChatGPT Baseline Package
workflows.reason: A single-use packaging job that zipped the working tree into a repo-source artifact so an external audit could read it. It was never on main: its only trigger was `on: push` restricted to the branch chatgpt/audit-remediation-20260809, it ran once on 2026-08-10 (run 31347624072, success, artifact retention 1 day, long expired), and the file was deleted from that branch afterwards. No ref in this repository contains it, so it cannot run again and there is nothing to invoke.
workflows.reinstateBy: Commit a workflow file at the recorded path and remove this entry. Nothing here suppresses a real workflow; the entry is a claim that no file exists, and validate_workflows.js fails if that claim stops being true.
